topic: Graphs of Linear Equations in the Form ax + by = k

lessonData.topic: Graphs of Linear Equations in the Form ax + by = k
lessonData.subject: Mathematics / Coordinate Geometry
lessonData.tagline: Master the standard linear form: transform equations, plot with precision, and unlock the Cartesian plane.
lessonData.overview: Every linear equation in the form ax + by = k maps directly to a straight line on the Cartesian plane by finding coordinate pairs that make the equation true. By rearranging it into gradient-intercept form or generating at least three test points, we can graph and analyze these equations with complete accuracy.

chalkNotes.title: Graphing ax + by = k
chalkNotes.subtitle: Standard Form & Graphing Rules
chalkNotes.coreRuleOrFormula: ax + by = k  ⟹  by = -ax + k  ⟹  y = (-a/b)x + (k/b)
bulletPoints: Dividing by b applies to EVERY term: watch out when b is negative (e.g., -3y = -2x + 6 gives y = 2/3 x - 2).
Always generate at least 3 points: if they do not lie on a single ruler edge, an algebraic or plotting error occurred.
A point (p, q) lies on the line if and only if substituting x = p and y = q makes the equation true (ap + bq = k).
Read coordinates from axis numbers, not physical centimetres (different scales like 1 cm = 1 unit on x and 2 cm = 1 unit on y are already marked for you).
keyTakeaways: Rearranging reveals the gradient (-a/b) and y-intercept (k/b) immediately.
Horizontal lines have the form y = c, intersecting ax + by = k where y equals c.

quiz.question: When rearranging the linear equation 2x - 3y = 6 into the gradient-intercept form y = mx + c, what are the correct values for the gradient m and y-intercept c?
quiz.explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides to get -3y = -2x + 6. Next, divide every single term by -3: y = (-2/-3)x + (6/-3). Because a negative divided by a negative is positive, the gradient is m = 2/3. Dividing +6 by -3 gives c = -2. Forgetting to divide the constant by the negative sign is a very common trap!

suggestedQuestions: What is the equation of a horizontal line passing through (0, 4), and how does it intersect 2x - 3y = 2?
If a grid uses 2 cm to represent 1 unit on the y-axis, why shouldn't I multiply my calculated y-coordinate by 2 before locating it?
If 3x + y = 7, what is the value of y when x = 2, and how do we check if (2, 1) lies on the line?

nodes.label: Intercept Method
nodes.details: Substitute x = 0 to calculate the y-intercept (0, k/b), then substitute y = 0 to calculate the x-intercept (k/a, 0).

nodes.label: Linear Equation ax + by = k
nodes.details: Defines a straight line on the Cartesian plane where a, b, and k are constants, and a and b are not both zero.

nodes.label: Coordinate Intercepts
nodes.details: Easily plotted using the cover-up method: set y = 0 to find the x-intercept, and set x = 0 to find the y-intercept.

nodes.label: Line Slope
nodes.details: Governs the steepness and direction; if a and b share the same sign, the line slopes downward from left to right.

nodes.label: Role of Constant k
nodes.details: Varying k shifts the line parallel to itself; when k = 0, the line passes directly through the origin (0, 0).

steps.name: Find the x-intercept
steps.caption: When y = 0, 2(1) - 3(0) = 2, giving the intercept point (1, 0).

steps.caption: A third point (4, 2) checks our arithmetic before ruling a line.
